message.content:
You are writing a concrete EXECUTION PLAN for a secondary-income business for Hooman (Adobe eng manager; $25-150K capital; ~10-20 hrs/wk alongside a day job; wants $5-30K/mo; already building CutLog).

IDEA: "Vertical bookkeeping / financial-ops subscription (one industry)"

The deep-research/validation stage produced these findings (JSON) — BUILD THE PLAN AROUND THE VALIDATED REALITY, not the original optimistic pitch:
{
  "idea": "Vertical bookkeeping / financial-ops subscription — pick one industry, get QuickBooks ProAdvisor certified, land 10-20 clients at $500-1,000/mo, systematize the monthly close, and delegate execution to trained bookkeepers/VAs while keeping a day job.",
  "slug": "vertical_bookkeeping",
  "assumptions_checked": [
    {
      "claim": "Boringest / safest / most durable business",
      "status": "PARTIALLY-TRUE",
      "evidence": "Demand is genuinely durable and non-cyclical (every business needs books). But 'safe' collides with heavy commoditization (thousands of local firms + offshore floor at $8-20/hr + venture players $99-599/mo) and active AI compression of the exact task being sold. Durable as a category, not obviously safe/defensible as a unit. Bench pricing bench.co/pricing (live); Pilot pilot.com/pricing (live)."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Fully delegable to trained bookkeepers/VAs",
      "status": "PARTIALLY-TRUE",
      "evidence": "The LABOR (categorization/reconciliation/close) delegates cleanly — Bench/Pilot/Bookkeeper360 do it at scale (Bench had ~650 employees). But SALES, QA/review (a bad close misstates taxes = trust+liability event), and retention do NOT delegate early, and delegation costs 35-60% of revenue. Wikipedia Bench timeline (live)."
    },
    {
      "claim": "$5-15K/mo with 10-20 clients",
      "status": "PARTIALLY-TRUE",
      "evidence": "Revenue math holds: at verified $300-1,500/mo/client, 10-20 clients = ~$5-20K/mo GROSS. But pitch reads it as PROFIT. After delegated labor + software + E&O + CAC, net at 15 clients (~$10.5K gross) is ~$4.5-8K/mo, not $10-15K. Top of range is best-case (20+ retained + cheap offshore + zero ongoing CAC). Vendor pricing pages (live)."
    },
    {
      "claim": "<$50K capital",
      "status": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Near-zero hard capital: QBO Accountant is free to ProAdvisors, add-ons in low $100s/mo, labor payable from client cash. Many firms start for <$5K; the $25-50K is a runway/marketing buffer, not required outlay. This is the idea's single best attribute. quickbooks.intuit.com/accountants/training-certification (live)."
    },
    {
      "claim": "QuickBooks ProAdvisor cert = a weekend",
      "status": "PARTIALLY-TRUE",
      "evidence": "The QBO ProAdvisor cert is FREE, self-paced, with annual recert — passable in a weekend of study (quickbooks.intuit.com/accountants/training-certification, live). But the cert is a software-proficiency badge, NOT competence to run client books. Real competence (accrual, sales-tax nexus, payroll, trust accounting, vertical rules) takes months and is where trust-killing errors happen. The badge was never the barrier."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Bookkeeping-as-a-service is a safe, proven, high-margin model",
      "status": "FALSE",
      "evidence": "Bench raised $100M+ (through a $60M Series C, Bain/Altos/Contour/iNovia), reached ~650 employees, and still imploded overnight Dec 27 2024 — bankruptcy Jan 2025 with $65.4M liabilities vs $2.8M cash, then fire-sold to Employer.com. $100M+ of smart money could not make the model durably profitable. Wikipedia Bench Accounting (live) + TechCrunch Dec 2024."
    }
  ],
  "competitors": [
    "Bench — DTC SMB bookkeeping; $199/399/599/mo + $55/hr option; raised $100M+; shut down Dec 27 2024 ($65.4M liabilities, ~650 staff), acquired by Employer.com Dec 30 2024",
    "Pilot — startup/SMB bookkeeping+tax; Essentials $99/mo, Core custom; ships 'instant AI answers'; backed by Sequoia/Index/Stripe/Bezos, ~$100M+ raised at ~$1.2B valuation",
    "Bookkeeper360 — multi-vertical (ecommerce/SaaS/healthcare/real estate); Monthly $399/mo, Weekly $599/mo, onboarding from $1,000; proprietary dashboard",
    "Bookkeeper.law — law-firm vertical; $2,327/mo full-time or $14/hr",
    "Accounting Atelier — attorneys; solo $600-800/mo, small firms $1,000-1,500/mo",
    "Firm Balance — attorney/multi-attorney bookkeeping",
    "Remote Books Online — lawyer vertical $300-900/mo; general SMB",
    "MBS Accountancy — dental CPA + monthly bookkeeping (dental is a saturated 'dental CPA' niche)",
    "Offshore/commodity floor — Fiverr/Upwork freelancers + Philippines/India BPOs at ~$8-20/hr; plus Xendoo, Bookkeeper.com, 1-800Accountant, and thousands of local firms"
  ],
  "economics_verified": "Price per client VERIFIED at $300-1,500/mo (horizontal $199-599; niche law/dental/ecommerce $500-1,500). Realistic steady-state P&L at 15 clients @ ~$700/mo = ~$10.5K/mo GROSS; minus delegated labor (offshore ~$75/client ≈ $1,125), software ($300-600), E&O+misc ($200-400), and amortized CAC during growth ($500-1,500) → NET ~$4.5-8K/mo at maturity, ~$4.5-6K/mo if delegated to US labor or still spending on growth. CHANGED vs pitch: the '$5-15K/mo' was read as profit but is really gross; realistic profit is ~$4.5-8K/mo (only the LOW end of the pitch is right; $12-15K is best-case, not expected). Capital CONFIRMED <$50K (actually can be <$10K) — the strongest attribute. Ramp: the pitch omits a 12-24 month personal SALES grind to fill 15-20 retained seats, in Hooman's scarce hours, plus baseline churn to out-run.",
  "verdict": "PASS",
  "confidence": "MEDIUM",
  "kill_risks": [
    "Sales/distribution gate is Hooman's KNOWN weakness: 0→15 clients is a 12-24mo personal sales grind competing directly with CutLog for his scarce best hours — Track-B report §5 explicitly warns against opening a second front that needs him to personally grind sales. Nearly disqualifying for a SECONDARY stream.",
    "Thin moat + commoditization: offshore floor at $8-20/hr, venture players at $99-599/mo, thousands of local firms. Bench raised $100M+ and still died — the category's economics are a caution, not a green light.",
    "AI/automation compression: incumbents (Pilot 'instant AI answers', Intuit/QuickBooks Live) are actively productizing AI to shrink the billable close; BLS treats the occupation as declining (~-5% 2023-33, flagged UNVERIFIED live). The service sold is the exact thing AI is eating — arguably INSIDE the AI-hype arena the mandate says to avoid.",
    "Trust/liability delegation trap: one bad close that misstates taxes loses a client and invites claims; owner must own QA for a long time, so it is NOT hands-off early. E&O insurance mandatory.",
    "Profit < pitch: net ~$4.5-8K/mo at 15 clients, not $10-15K; top of range is best-case only.",
    "Low founder-fit / not his domain: real competence is months of learning (payroll, sales-tax nexus, trust accounting), not a weekend cert."
  ],
  "best_niche_or_target": "Bookkeeping + financial-ops for small SaaS / indie-software / digital-product businesses (Stripe/Paddle/App-Store revenue, deferred-revenue recognition, MRR/ARR reporting, multi-currency, R&D expense tracking). Rationale: Hooman natively understands these businesses and metrics; the pain (rev-rec, Stripe reconciliation, MRR reporting) is under-served by generalist bookkeepers; it overlaps his CutLog/indie-hacker network for distribution; and it justifies premium pricing ($800-1,500/mo) + advisory upsell. AVOID the obvious saturated verticals (dental, law/trust-accounting, general ecommerce, restaurants, real estate) — all already owned by entrenched niche firms. Caveat: even this best niche only improves win-rate/pricing; it does not change the thin-moat, sales-gated, delegation-compresses-margin shape.",
  "_idea": {
    "slug": "vertical_bookkeeping",
    "name": "Vertical bookkeeping / financial-ops subscription (one industry)",
    "claims": "Boringest/safest/most durable; fully delegable to trained bookkeepers/VAs; $5-15K/mo with 10-20 clients; <$50K capital; QuickBooks ProAdvisor cert = a weekend. Key open questions: which vertical? realistic client acquisition cost + churn? can it truly be delegated while Hooman keeps a day job? competitive density (Bench, Pilot, Bookkeeper360, thousands of local firms)?"
  }
}

Also read your own research doc at /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/runs/trackB/deep/vertical_bookkeeping/01_research_validation.md for detail.

Write a concrete, realistic execution plan:
  - The specific target (exact niche/exam/tool/vertical/acquisition profile chosen in research).
  - First 90 days: week-by-week concrete actions, who does what, what gets validated when.
  - Months 4-12: path to the revenue target, hiring/delegation plan (this MUST stay part-time for Hooman).
  - Itemized budget within $25-150K; monthly burn; break-even point.
  - Revenue model + realistic ramp curve (subscribers/clients/deals over time).
  - Concrete go/no-go decision gates and the cheapest possible validation BEFORE committing real money.
  - How it coexists with CutLog for Hooman's limited hours (capital+delegation vs focus).

WRITE the plan to /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/runs/trackB/deep/vertical_bookkeeping/02_execution_plan.md (use Write). Return a ~200-word summary of the plan as your final text.

1	# Deep Research + Assumption Validation — Vertical Bookkeeping / Financial-Ops Subscription
2	
3	**Idea (Track-B #3, scored 8.15):** Pick ONE industry vertical, get QuickBooks ProAdvisor
4	certified, land 10–20 clients at $500–1,000/mo, deliver a systematized monthly close, and
5	delegate the execution to trained bookkeepers/VAs while Hooman keeps his Adobe day job.
6	
7	**Researcher stance:** skeptic. Every pitch claim is verified against real sources below and
8	marked VERIFIED / PARTIALLY-TRUE / FALSE / UNVERIFIED.
9	
10	**Date:** 2026-07-01. **Owner:** Hooman Shariati.
11	
12	**Research-tooling caveat:** general search engines (Google/Bing/DDG) were rate-limited /
13	CAPTCHA-blocked during this session, and several industry blogs (Jetpack Workflow, Upwork
14	resources, BLS) returned 403/404 to the fetch bot. Where a specific number could not be
15	pulled from a live page it is marked UNVERIFIED and flagged as "well-established but not
16	re-fetched this session." Primary vendor pricing pages (Bench, Pilot, Bookkeeper360) and
17	Wikipedia's sourced Bench timeline WERE fetched live and are cited.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## 1. Claim-by-claim verification
22	
23	### Claim A — "Boringest / safest / most durable"
24	**Verdict: PARTIALLY-TRUE (durable-yes, safe-with-caveats).**
25	- Bookkeeping is genuinely boring and non-cyclical — every business with revenue needs books,
26	  and the need does not evaporate in a downturn. Durable demand: TRUE.
27	- BUT "safest" collides with two structural pressures documented below: (1) heavy price
28	  competition from thousands of local firms + offshore + venture-backed players, and (2)
29	  active automation/AI compression of the very task being sold. It is durable as an *industry*
30	  but not obviously "safe" as a *differentiated, defensible, high-margin* niche business.
31	- The Track-B report itself rates durability 9/10; that is defensible for the *category* but
32	  the report under-weights competitive density and AI compression at the *unit* level.
33	
34	### Claim B — "Fully delegable to trained bookkeepers/VAs"
35	**Verdict: PARTIALLY-TRUE.**
36	- The *execution* (transaction categorization, reconciliation, monthly close) is genuinely
37	  delegable — this is exactly what Bench, Pilot, and Bookkeeper360 do at scale with teams of
38	  bookkeepers (Bench had ~650 employees at closure; source: Wikipedia/Bench timeline, fetched
39	  live). Delegability of the labor: VERIFIED.
40	- What is NOT delegable early on: (a) SALES / client acquisition — the founder's scarce time
41	  is spent here, and this is precisely Hooman's known weakness (see Track-B report §5); (b)
42	  the review/QA layer — a bookkeeping error that misstates a client's taxes is a
43	  trust-and-liability event, so the owner must own final review until a senior lead is trusted;
44	  (c) client relationship / retention. So "fully delegable" overstates it: the *commodity
45	  labor* delegates cleanly; the *two things that actually make or break the business*
46	  (getting clients, not losing them to errors) do not delegate for a long time.
47	- Delegation ALSO compresses margin. See economics (§4): a US$500–1,000/mo client whose work
48	  is delegated to a US bookkeeper at ~$25–45/hr, or an offshore bookkeeper at ~$8–20/hr,
49	  leaves a real but modest per-client margin, not a software-like 90%.
50	
51	### Claim C — "$5–15K/mo with 10–20 clients"
52	**Verdict: PARTIALLY-TRUE on gross revenue; MISLEADING on profit.**
53	- Arithmetic checks on *revenue*: at the real market price points confirmed below
54	  ($300–1,500/mo/client for niche/small-biz bookkeeping), 10–20 clients = roughly
55	  $5K–$20K/mo gross. So the top-line range is plausible. VERIFIED that the *price per client*
56	  supports it.
57	- But the pitch quietly reads the $5–15K as *profit* ("$5–15K/mo"). Once you subtract the
58	  delegated bookkeeper labor, software (QBO/QBO Accountant, ledger tools, workpaper apps),
59	  E&O insurance, and any paid acquisition, net margin on a delegated book is more like
60	  40–65%, not ~100%. Realistic *profit* at 15 clients averaging ~$700/mo ($10.5K gross) is
61	  closer to **$4.5–6.5K/mo net**, not $10–15K — and that assumes clients are already landed
62	  and retained. See §4.
63	- Survivorship-bias check: the "$X/mo with N clients" figure is an *at-steady-state* number.
64	  It ignores the 12–24 month ramp to fill 15–20 retained seats, during which the owner is
65	  doing unpaid sales. This is the same survivorship trap the Track-B report flagged for
66	  micro-SaaS (LEARNINGS: ~5% reach $5–20K/mo) — it applies to service firms too, just less
67	  severely because demand is real.
68	
69	### Claim D — "<$50K capital"
70	**Verdict: VERIFIED (arguably generous — it can be far less).**
71	- A bookkeeping practice is close to zero hard-capital. Software subscriptions (QBO
72	  Accountant is free to ProAdvisors; add-ons/workpaper/receipt tools run low $100s/mo),
73	  a website, E&O insurance, and *labor you can pay out of client cash* once revenue starts.
74	  Many bookkeeping firms are started for <$5K. The $25–50K in the scorecard is mostly a
75	  runway/marketing buffer, not required outlay. Capital fit: strongly VERIFIED. This is the
76	  idea's single best attribute.
77	
78	### Claim E — "QuickBooks ProAdvisor cert = a weekend"
79	**Verdict: PARTIALLY-TRUE — the CERT is easy and free; the COMPETENCE is not a weekend.**
80	- The QuickBooks Online ProAdvisor certification is **free** and self-paced through the
81	  ProAdvisor Academy; there is an exam with periodic (annual) recertification (source:
82	  quickbooks.intuit.com/accountants/training-certification, fetched live — confirms free
83	  self-paced training + recert exam; it does not publish a fee, consistent with "free for
84	  QBOA members"). Passing the online cert in a weekend of study: plausibly TRUE.
85	- BUT the cert is a *software-proficiency* badge, not a license to competently run a client's
86	  books. Real competence — accrual vs cash, chart-of-accounts design, sales-tax nexus,
87	  payroll liabilities, month-end close discipline, catch-up/cleanup engagements, and the
88	  vertical's specific rules (e.g. law-firm trust/IOLTA accounting, restaurant tip/COGS,
89	  e-commerce multi-channel + inventory + sales-tax) — takes months and is where the errors
90	  that kill trust happen. "ProAdvisor = a weekend" is TRUE and irrelevant; the barrier was
91	  never the badge. This is a knowledge business, and Hooman starts at zero domain knowledge
92	  (the Track-B report concedes founder-fit here is "low").
93	
94	---
95	
96	## 2. Real competitors (named, with pricing / scale / funding)
97	
98	**Venture-backed / national horizontal players (the price and expectation setters):**
99	
100	- **Bench** — DTC small-business bookkeeping. Pricing (bench.co/pricing, fetched live):
101	  Grow $199/mo, Core $399/mo, Core+Tax $599/mo, plus a $55/hr QBO-certified option with a
102	  $1,200 onboarding fee. **Raised $100M+** (seed→$60M Series C in 2021; investors incl. Bain
103	  Capital Ventures, Altos, Contour, iNovia). **Abruptly shut down Dec 27, 2024**, filed
104	  bankruptcy in Canada Jan 7 2025 with **$65.4M liabilities vs $2.8M cash**, ~650 employees,
105	  then was acquired by **Employer.com** Dec 30 2024 and restarted (source: Wikipedia Bench
106	  timeline, fetched live; corroborated by contemporaneous TechCrunch coverage).
107	  **This is the single most important finding in this report** — see §3.
108	
109	- **Pilot** — startup/SMB bookkeeping + tax. Pricing (pilot.com/pricing, fetched live):
110	  Essentials $99/mo (≤$100K/mo expenses), Core (custom, "$0 base billed annually"), Custom.
111	  Explicitly ships **"Instant AI answers about past transactions and current cash flow"** —
112	  i.e. an incumbent is already productizing AI into the offering. Backed by Sequoia, Index,
113	  Stripe, Bezos Expeditions; raised **$100M+ at a ~$1.2B valuation (2021)**. Positions as
114	  "the largest startup and small business accounting firm in the US."
115	
116	- **Bookkeeper360** — SMB + multi-vertical (ecommerce, SaaS, healthcare, real estate).
117	  Pricing (bookkeeper360.com/pricing, fetched live): Monthly from $399/mo, Weekly from
118	  $599/mo, onboarding/catch-up from $1,000. Proprietary dashboard + app.
119	
120	**Named vertical / niche firms (the direct competitors for the "one industry" strategy):**
121	
122	- **Law firms:** Bookkeeper.law ($2,327/mo full-time or $14/hr), Firm Balance, Accounting
123	  Atelier (solo attys $600–800/mo; small firms $1,000–1,500/mo), Remote Books Online lawyer
124	  vertical ($300–900/mo) (source: DDG result set, fetched live). Law is *already* a mature,
125	  competed vertical with trust-accounting specialists.
126	- **Dentists:** MBS Accountancy (dental CPA + monthly bookkeeping) and many "dental CPA"
127	  practices; dentistry is one of the most saturated bookkeeping niches (long-standing
128	  "dental CPA" cottage industry).
129	- **E-commerce:** Bookkeeper360 ecommerce vertical, plus specialist firms (e.g. A2X-partner
130	  ecommerce bookkeepers) — a crowded, sophisticated niche (multi-channel, inventory,
131	  sales-tax nexus).
132	- **General/offshore commodity floor:** Remote Books Online, Bookkeeper.com, Xendoo, 1-800
133	  Accountant, plus thousands of local firms and Fiverr/Upwork freelancers, and offshore BPOs
134	  that will keep books for **$8–20/hr**.
135	
136	**Competitive-density read:** this is a **crowded, mature, commoditized** market with a
137	venture-funded top, a specialist-vertical middle that is ALREADY occupied (law, dental,
138	ecommerce, restaurant, trucking, real estate, agencies, medical, nonprofits all have
139	established niche players), and an offshore price floor at the bottom. Every "obvious" good
140	vertical is taken. This is the opposite of the Track-A "underserved mid-market" archetype the
141	project keeps looking for.
142	
143	---
144	
145	## 3. The Bench signal — read this before pursuing
146	
147	A bookkeeping company that raised **>$100M**, reached ~650 employees and (reportedly) ~11,000+
148	SMB customers, still **ran out of cash and imploded overnight in Dec 2024**. Takeaways:
149	
150	1. **Bookkeeping-as-a-service is a low-margin, high-ops, high-churn grind even at scale.**
151	   $100M+ of the smartest venture money could not make the horizontal DTC model durably
152	   profitable. That is a screaming caution, not a green light, for a solo operator.
153	2. **The moat is thin.** Bench's customers were portable; when it died, competitors (incl.
154	   Pilot and QuickBooks Live) immediately courted them. A niche solo firm's moat (relationship
155	   + vertical know-how) is realer than Bench's but still rests on the owner, not the asset.
156	3. **AI is being productized by the incumbents right now.** Pilot ships "instant AI answers";
157	   QuickBooks/Intuit is pushing AI categorization and "QuickBooks Live"; the whole point of
158	   the tooling is to compress the billable labor. The service is being squeezed from the
159	   software side. (Corroborating: US BLS classifies "bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing
160	   clerks" as a **declining occupation, projected roughly -5% over 2023–2033**, explicitly

162	   well-established, frequently-cited figure. Flag to re-confirm.)

164	The counter-argument (why a *niche* firm can still work): niche firms win on trust, vertical
165	fluency, and advisory upsell that Bench never delivered — they run at 40–65% net margins at
166	small scale precisely because they DON'T carry Bench's overhead or CAC. Bench's death is an
167	indictment of the *venture DTC* model, not of the *boutique niche* model. Both readings are
168	true; the honest synthesis is: **the boutique niche model is a viable modest-income business,
169	but it is a labor/relationship business with a thin moat, not the "safe, delegable,
170	near-passive, software-margin" thing the pitch implies.**

183	  transaction volume/complexity (industry rule-of-thumb; UNVERIFIED this session — the
184	  Jetpack/industry pages 404/403'd — but widely cited; flag to confirm).
185	- US bookkeeper labor ~$25–45/hr; offshore (Philippines/India) ~$8–20/hr (UNVERIFIED live

219	- **Avoid (already saturated by specialists):** dental, law/attorney (trust accounting is a

222	- **Best-fit specific niche for THIS founder:** a **technical / digital-native vertical where

# Execution Plan — Vertical Bookkeeping / Financial-Ops Subscription

**Owner:** Hooman Shariati · **Date:** 2026-07-01 · **Status:** conditional-go, sales-gated
**Companion:** `01_research_validation.md` (verdict: PASS-as-pitched; only one narrow form survives)

> **Read this first.** The research says a from-scratch bookkeeping firm is a PASS for Hooman
> as a *secondary* stream, for two reasons the plan cannot engineer away: (1) it needs his
> scarce personal SALES time — his known weakness, already claimed by CutLog; (2) the exact
> billable task is being eaten by incumbent AI (Pilot, QuickBooks Live). Bench raised $100M+
> and died. **Therefore this plan is deliberately front-loaded with a cheap $0–2K, ~40-hour
> "kill gate" that runs in parallel with CutLog and is designed to say NO fast.** Do not spend
> real money, hire anyone, or take a paying client until Gate 1 passes. The realistic upside if
> it fully works is **~$4.5–8K/mo net at 15 clients after a 12–24-month sales ramp** — modest,
> and only worth it if the Gate-1 validation shows selling is *easy* in the chosen niche.

---

## 1. The Specific Target (locked)

| Dimension | Decision | Why (from research §5) |
|---|---|---|
| **Vertical** | **Financial-ops for small SaaS / indie-software / digital-product businesses** ($0–3M ARR, Stripe/Paddle/App-Store revenue) | Only niche where Hooman's software fluency is a real edge; incumbents (generalist bookkeepers) are weak on rev-rec, Stripe reconciliation, MRR/ARR, multi-currency. Overlaps his CutLog / indie-hacker network for distribution. |
| **AVOID** | dental, law/attorney (trust/IOLTA), general ecommerce, restaurants, real estate, medical | All saturated by entrenched niche firms + CPAs (research §5). |
| **Positioning** | NOT "bookkeeping." **"Finance-ops for indie SaaS founders: clean books + Stripe/MRR reconciliation + investor-ready ARR reporting + rev-rec you can trust."** | Escapes the commoditized $199–599 horizontal price war; justifies premium. |
| **Price** | **$800–1,500/mo/client** (target avg ~$900), setup/catch-up $750–1,500 one-time | Niche complexity supports it (research §4). Do NOT compete with Bench/Pilot on price. |
| **Cert** | QuickBooks Online ProAdvisor (free, self-paced, ~1 weekend) + Stripe/A2X/Baremetrics fluency | Cert is a badge, not competence (research §E). The real prep is rev-rec + SaaS-metrics knowledge. |
| **Ideal client profile (ICP)** | Bootstrapped/small-VC SaaS, $10K–200K MRR, 1–3 founders, no in-house finance, uses Stripe, wants investor/board-ready numbers | Has money, has real pain, values software fluency, reachable in Hooman's network. |
| **Delegation model** | Founder owns SALES + QA/review + client relationship; **offshore/contract bookkeeper owns categorization/reconciliation/close** once >5 clients | Labor delegates; sales+QA+retention do not (research §B). |

**The single best attribute stays true:** capital need is near-zero (<$10K), so the risk is
Hooman's *time*, not his money. That is exactly why the gates below protect his time, not his cash.

---

## 2. How It Coexists With CutLog (the real constraint)

CutLog is the priority and already owns Hooman's builder hours. This idea must **never** compete
for the same deep-work block. Rules:

1. **CutLog first.** If in any week CutLog needs the hours, bookkeeping pauses. No exceptions
   during the Gate-1 validation phase.
2. **This is a "sell + delegate" business, not a "build" business** — its time cost is *sales &
   review*, which is different muscle from CutLog's product work but competes for the same
   scarce total hours. Budget **max 5–7 hrs/wk** to it during validation, rising to ~8–10 hrs/wk
   only *after* it earns revenue and a delegate is doing the labor.
3. **Distribution synergy, not distraction:** the same indie-SaaS/CutLog network is the lead
   source for both. Selling finance-ops to CutLog-adjacent founders can be done in the same
   conversations. Exploit that overlap; do not build a separate sales motion.
4. **Capital+delegation over founder-focus:** the moment it has ≥5 clients, push ALL labor to a
   contractor and Hooman's role shrinks to sales + weekly QA review (~4–5 hrs/wk). If it can't
   get to delegated-QA-only by ~month 9, it is failing the "secondary/part-time" test — kill or
   sell it.
5. **Hard stop:** if serving clients ever pulls Hooman below the CutLog hours he needs, the
   bookkeeping clients get transitioned to the delegate or handed off — CutLog wins.

---

## 3. Cheapest-Possible Validation BEFORE Any Real Money (the kill gate)

**Total spend to reach the first go/no-go: $0–200. Total time: ~30–40 hrs over 4–5 weeks.**
This exists because the research's #1 kill-risk is "can Hooman actually sell this?" Answer that
for ~$0 before touching QuickBooks certs, insurance, or contractors.

- **Offer test, not product test.** Sell the *promise* to 15–25 indie-SaaS founders in his
  network / Indie Hackers / relevant Slacks / X before doing any bookkeeping. Pitch: "I'm
  starting a finance-ops service for SaaS founders — clean books + Stripe reconciliation +
  board-ready MRR/ARR + rev-rec — $900/mo. Would you want this?"
- **Success = commitment, not compliments.** The bar is **≥3 founders who say "yes, I'd pay
  $800+/mo" and 1 who will start a paid pilot within 30 days.** Verbal "sounds great" counts as NO.
- Cost: a landing page (Carrd/free), calendar link, ~20 outreach conversations. $0–100.

---

## 4. First 90 Days — Week by Week

**Phase A — Validate the SALE (Weeks 1–5). Spend cap: $200. ~6 hrs/wk.**

| Week | Actions (Hooman unless noted) | Validated by end |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Write the ICP + one-page offer + pricing ($900/mo, $1K setup). Stand up a Carrd landing page + Cal.com link. List 30 target founders from his network/IH/X/Slacks. | Offer + list exist |
| 2 | 10–15 outreach DMs/emails/calls. Ask about their current bookkeeping pain (Stripe recon, rev-rec, MRR reporting), NOT a hard sell yet. | Pain confirmed or denied |
| 3 | 10–15 more conversations. Start floating price. Track: how many have real pain? how many balk at $800+? | Willingness-to-pay signal |
| 4 | Ask the warm ones directly for a paid pilot start within 30 days. Get a soft LOI / "yes I'd pay." | **GATE 1 (see §6)** |
| 5 | If Gate 1 passes: line up 1 paid pilot client. If not: STOP — write it up, return to CutLog. | Pilot client or kill |

**Phase B — Deliver ONE client yourself (Weeks 6–13). Only if Gate 1 passed. ~7 hrs/wk.**

| Week | Actions | Validated |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | Buy E&O insurance (~$50–100/mo). QBO Accountant (free). Complete ProAdvisor cert (weekend). Set up A2X/Stripe integration + a close checklist template. | Tooling ready |
| 7–8 | Onboard + catch-up the pilot client's books yourself. Time-track every hour ruthlessly. | Real hours/client known |
| 9–10 | Run first full monthly close for the pilot. Deliver an investor-ready MRR/ARR + rev-rec package. Get explicit feedback. | Deliverable quality |
| 11 | Land 1–2 more clients from the Week 1–4 warm list. | Repeatability |
| 12 | Hire + trial ONE offshore/contract bookkeeper (Upwork/BPO, ~$8–20/hr); hand them categorization+recon under Hooman's QA. | Delegation works |
| 13 | Review: hours/client, delegate quality, margin per client, whether sales felt easy or brutal. | **GATE 2 (see §6)** |

**Who does what:** Hooman = sales, QA/review, client relationship, all of Phase A/B delivery
until Week 12. Contractor = categorization + reconciliation under QA from Week 12. No employees, ever.

---

## 5. Months 4–12 — Path to Target (part-time, delegated)

Only if Gate 2 passes. The whole game now is: **sell steadily, keep Hooman out of the labor.**

| Month | Clients (retained) | Hooman's role | Delegate | Gross/mo | Net/mo |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 (end P-B) | 2–3 | full delivery + sales | trialing | ~$2.4K | ~$1–1.5K |
| 6 | 5–7 | sales + weekly QA only | 1 contractor (labor) | ~$5–6K | ~$2.5–3.5K |
| 9 | 8–11 | sales + QA (~4–5 hr/wk) | 1 contractor scaling | ~$7.5–10K | ~$4–6K |
| 12 | 12–16 | sales + QA + a senior lead for overflow | 1–2 contractors | ~$11–14K | **~$4.5–8K** |

- **Hiring/delegation plan:** contractors only, paid from client cash, never W-2 employees.
  One offshore bookkeeper carries ~15–40 clients depending on complexity (research §4, flagged
  UNVERIFIED — confirm in Phase B by measuring real hours). Add a second/senior contractor for
  QA-assist only when >12 clients so Hooman's review load stays ≤5 hrs/wk.
- **Sales:** ~1 net-new retained client/month via network + referrals + niche communities.
  This is the fragile assumption. Referrals from happy SaaS founders are the cheapest channel;
  paid ads are a last resort (bad CAC in this space).
- **Churn:** assume ~2–3%/mo baseline (clients get acquired, go in-house, or leave over one bad
  close). Selling ~1/mo net *includes* out-running churn.
- **Part-time guarantee:** if at any point Hooman's weekly hours exceed ~10 or CutLog suffers,
  the response is *more delegation / slower sales / raise prices*, NOT more of Hooman's time.

---

## 6. Go / No-Go Decision Gates

- **GATE 1 (end Week 4) — the sale.** GO only if **≥3 founders say they'd pay $800+/mo AND ≥1
  commits to a paid pilot within 30 days**, gathered without begging. If not → **KILL. Total
  cost <$200, ~25 hrs.** This is the whole point of the plan: fail cheap on Hooman's weakness.
- **GATE 2 (end Week 13) — the unit + delegation.** GO only if: (a) client accepts the monthly
  package and renews; (b) per-client delivery ≤6 hrs *and* successfully handed to a contractor
  under QA; (c) net margin per client ≥40%; (d) at least 2–3 paying clients; (e) sales felt
  *repeatable*, not soul-crushing. If any fails → freeze at current clients, do not scale, or exit.
- **GATE 3 (month 9) — the part-time test.** GO to keep scaling only if Hooman's personal time
  is ≤5 hrs/wk (labor fully delegated, QA-only) AND net ≥$4K/mo AND CutLog unharmed. If Hooman is
  still doing labor or sales is stalling → this is not a viable secondary stream; **hand clients to
  the delegate as a lifestyle micro-book, or sell the small book, and return focus to CutLog.**

---

## 7. Budget (within $25–150K; actual need is far lower)

**Capital is this idea's best attribute — the real budget is tiny; the "$25–150K" is unused buffer.**

| Item | One-time | Monthly | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Landing page / domain / Cal.com | $0–50 | ~$0–20 | Carrd/free tier |
| QBO Accountant + ProAdvisor cert | $0 | $0 | Free to ProAdvisors |
| E&O / professional-liability insurance | — | ~$50–100 | Mandatory before first client |
| Add-ons: A2X, receipt/workpaper, close tool | — | ~$100–300 | Scales with clients |
| Offshore/contract bookkeeper | — | ~$75/client (starts month 3) | Paid from client cash |
| Misc (payment fees, subs, small ads test) | — | ~$100–300 | |
| **Cash needed before break-even** | **~$1–3K** | **~$300–600 fixed pre-labor** | Everything else pays from revenue |

- **Monthly burn (pre-revenue):** ~$150–300. **Post-first-client:** labor scales with revenue.
- **Break-even:** essentially at **client #1** (a $900 client covers all fixed monthly cost).
  Cash-flow positive by ~month 3. The scarce resource is *Hooman's hours*, not dollars.
- **Discretionary buffer:** hold ~$5–10K for a small paid-acquisition experiment ONLY if
  organic/referral sales prove too slow after month 6 — and expect poor CAC (research §2). Do not
  deploy the $25–150K envelope; this business does not need it.

---

## 8. Revenue Model + Realistic Ramp

- **Model:** monthly recurring subscription ($800–1,500/mo) + one-time setup/catch-up
  ($750–1,500) + optional advisory upsell (board-deck / fundraise-prep, $500–2K project).
- **Ramp curve (retained clients):** 1 (mo 2) → 2–3 (mo 3) → 5–7 (mo 6) → 8–11 (mo 9) →
  12–16 (mo 12). ~1 net-new/mo after out-running churn.
- **Steady-state (mo 12–18, ~15 clients @ ~$900):** ~$11–14K/mo gross → **~$4.5–8K/mo net**
  (offshore-delegated, CAC tapered). This is the honest ceiling for a part-time operation; the
  pitch's "$10–15K/mo" is best-case (20+ retained + cheap offshore + zero CAC), not expected.

---

## 9. One-Paragraph Recommendation

Run **only Phase A** now, in the seams around CutLog, for <$200 and ~25 hours. It directly tests
the single thing that kills this idea for Hooman — whether *he* can sell finance-ops to SaaS
founders without a grind. If Gate 1 fails (the likely outcome given his profile and the AI-
compression / commoditization headwinds), he has lost almost nothing and confirmed CutLog is the
right sole focus. If Gate 1 surprisingly passes — meaning selling to his own indie-SaaS network is
*easy* — then and only then invest the weekend cert + first client, and scale strictly via
delegation so it stays a ≤5-hr/wk, capital-light, ~$4.5–8K/mo side stream that never steals CutLog's
hours. Do **not** start with the cert, insurance, or a contractor; start with the sale.
